storm.summary_layperson: A band of showers and embedded storms is moving through Greenwich right now and should clear the immediate area by early evening, but strong, gusty north-northeast wind under an active Wind Advisory continues through the whole 5-10 PM window as the front exits — the Sound isn't providing any extra buffer tonight, so conditions here will track with surrounding towns.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound (65.8°F) is actually warmer than the air (59°F) right now — the reverse of the setup a protective marine layer needs — so there's no stabilizing buffer in play for this window at all.
storm.detail_html:
A cold frontal band is moving through the Riverside/Greenwich area right now, producing periods of rain and embedded showers with radar reflectivity in the 35–41 dBZ range within a few miles of the cove. CAPE is 0 J/kg, meaning there's no real atmospheric instability driving this — it's frontal rain and gusty wind, not classic thunderstorm risk, despite the NWS text mentioning "isolated thunderstorms."

A Wind Advisory is in effect from 1:47 PM today through 6:15 AM tomorrow, covering the entire 5–10 PM window. NWS is calling for north wind around 24 mph with gusts to 40 mph today, consistent with HRRR and station data showing sustained 15–16 kt with gusts into the mid-20s. A Coastal Flood Warning is also active but expires right at 5 PM, at the start of this window, so it shouldn't be a factor for the evening.

The convective cells radar is currently tracking near the cove are moving through now — closing speeds mostly under 5 kt, and one cell is already past — rather than heading into the 5–10 PM window. By the time the window opens, the rain band should largely have cleared the immediate area, leaving the steady gradient wind behind it.

Local effect: neutral. The marine-layer mechanism that sometimes shields the cove is not in play tonight — warm water under cool air is the reverse of what's needed to build a stabilizing layer, so the protective-mechanism score is 0. Greenwich should see conditions in line with surrounding towns rather than any local buffering.

What would change this call: any new discrete cell developing behind the front with real CAPE, or an upgrade to a Severe Thunderstorm Warning — worth a radar recheck if wind or rain intensifies noticeably after 6 PM.

wind.tactics_blurb: Strong post-frontal N/NNE gradient wind holds all evening (no sea breeze in play) — steady 14-16 kt with gusts to 25, easing gradually toward 12-13 kt by 10 PM. Pressure is fairly even across the cove in this direction; stay centered and play the puffs rather than the shifts.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a strong gradient wind day — no sea breeze in play (B-strong). The land-water temperature gap is actually negative (air 59°F vs Sound 65.8°F), so there's no thermal driver at all tonight; the wind you get is entirely synoptic. The authoritative airport/well-sited-station average is 19.3 kt, comfortably above the 15 kt threshold for a big-breeze day.

HRRR's raw forecast direction for the window sits at N–NNE (10–15°), but live coastal observations are running more easterly — RYC reads NNE 20°, and the western-LIS station ensemble median is NE 42°, a 32° divergence from the model. Expect the true cove direction to sit somewhere between N and NE through the evening; watch RYC's live reading rather than leaning hard on the HRRR number.

Per the cove geography table, both NE and N/NNE flow tend to produce fairly even pressure across the cove, with the best average pressure sitting mid-course rather than tight to either shore — so favor the center of the course rather than committing hard to one side.

Shift character is persistent, not oscillating — this is post-frontal synoptic flow, not a thermal sea breeze, so there's no cyclical shift to play. Expect a steady direction with normal gust/lull cycling.

Speed should ease gradually through the window, from about 16 kt at 5 PM down to 12–13 kt by 10 PM, with gusts easing from the mid-20s into the high teens — consistent with the HRRR trend and B-strong's tendency to hold through sunset rather than collapse. HRRR data only extends to 7 PM this cycle; the 8–10 PM figures are extrapolated from the observed trend and carry lower confidence.

data_caveats: HRRR forecast hours f05-f12 (8-10 PM) were unavailable from this model cycle; those wind-table rows are trend-extrapolated, not model output.
Several regional METAR stations (KBDR, KHPN, KHVN, KGON, KISP, KFRG) have wind sensors offline; the ensemble leans more heavily on RYC, buoy 44040, and APRS stations.
HRRR forecast wind direction (N, ~10°) diverges from live coastal observations (NE, ~30-45°) by up to 32° — direction confidence may shift hour to hour.
